name: Risk Register
purpose: Captures the details of each identified individual risk and carries it through risk analysis, response planning, response implementation and current status, so risks can be tracked over the whole project. It is developed at the start of the project and updated throughout.

elements.guidance: A unique identifier for the risk. The blank form prints the column as ID.
The risk event or condition. Usually phrased 'EVENT may occur, causing IMPACT' or 'If CONDITION exists, EVENT may occur, leading to EFFECT'.
The person responsible for managing and tracking the risk. The blank form prints the column as Owner.
The likelihood of the event or condition occurring.
The effect on one or more project objectives. The blank form prints one Impact group with four columns: Scope, Quality, Schedule and Cost.
With numeric scoring, multiply probability by impact. With relative scoring, combine the two ratings (for example high-low or medium-high).
The planned response strategy for the risk or condition. The prose names no strategies here; the technique names come from PMBOK 6 chapter 11.
The likelihood of the event or condition after the response has been implemented.
The impact once the response has been implemented. In the blank form it is the second Impact group in the second bank (Scope, Quality, Schedule, Cost), printed as Impact, not Revised Impact.
The risk score after the response has been implemented.
Any actions that must be taken to respond to the risk.
Any comments or other helpful information about the risk event or condition.

citation: Book of Forms form 2.32, PDF pages 139 to 140 (printed pages 128 to 129); Table 2.29 PDF page 140 (printed page 129)
notes: Blank form: PDF page 141 (printed page 130). The book prints no Tailoring Tips and no Alignment section for this form, so tailoring and alignment are empty; for the documents to compare use the receives_from and provides_to lists. The blank form prints a Responsible Party column (bank 2) that Table 2.29 does not list, and prints ID and Owner where Table 2.29 says Risk ID and Risk owner; the blank form wins for labels. The prose says the register is 'an output from process 11.2 Identify Risks'. 'Scope baseline' and 'Schedule baseline' are not single forms (the baselines are made of several forms), so they are named, not numbered. 'Project closeout' in the provides_to list is taken to be form 5.2 Project or Phase Closeout; the prose does not give a number.
